title: Te Whāriki Manawāhine o Hauraki
subtitle: Branding & Visual Identity
description: Proposed Visual Identity Guidelines for Te Whāriki Manawāhine o Hauraki - a cultural design project celebrating Māori women's patterns and traditions from Hauraki.

sections.label: Overview
paragraphs: Te Whāriki Manawāhine o Hauraki represents a visual identity system developed to celebrate and preserve traditional Māori women's patterns from the Hauraki region. This project explores the intersection between cultural heritage and contemporary design, creating a visual system that honors tradition while being applicable to modern contexts.

The visual system draws inspiration from traditional weaving patterns (whāriki), natural forms of the Hauraki landscape, and significant cultural symbols to create an identity deeply rooted in the past while looking toward the future.

sections.label: Typography System
sections.html:
The typography system combines two complementary typefaces: Cormorant Garamond for display and heading text, and DM Sans for body text and labels. This pairing creates a balance between classical elegance and contemporary readability.

Display / Heading

Cormorant Garamond

Display/H1: Light 300

Heading/H2: Regular 400

Body & Labels

DM Sans

Body Text: Light 300 · 15px · line-height 1.8

Label/Tag: Bold 400 · 8px · tracked

Haere Mai

A place of healing, story, and connection.

sections.label: Pattern System
paragraphs: The pattern system draws inspiration from traditional whāriki (weaving) patterns, adapting geometric forms and rhythmic repetitions to create a contemporary visual language that respects cultural heritage while functioning in modern applications.

sections.label: Applications
paragraphs: The visual identity has been developed for various applications, from cultural documentation and educational materials to contemporary branding and digital platforms. Each application respects the core principles while adapting to specific contexts.
